name: Kadesh-barnea

identification.note: Usually identified with the oasis of Ain el-Qudeirat in the northern Sinai/Negev border area.

related_people.name: Ammiel
related_people.role: the spy from the tribe of Dan who brought back a fearful report of Canaan

related_people.name: Caleb
related_people.role: urged Israel from here to go up and take the land, and was promised Hebron

related_people.name: Igal
related_people.role: the spy from the tribe of Issachar who joined the fearful report of the land

description: A wilderness oasis that served as Israel's main base during much of the forty years of wandering. The twelve spies returned there with their report of Canaan (Numbers 13:26), and it was at Kadesh that Moses, in frustration, struck the rock instead of speaking to it as commanded — an act of disobedience that cost him entry into the promised land (Numbers 20:1-13).
family_friendly_summary: Kadesh-barnea was a desert oasis that served as Israel's main camp during much of their forty years in the wilderness. The twelve spies came back there with their report about Canaan. It was also where Moses disobeyed God by striking a rock instead of speaking to it, which meant he would not get to lead the people into the promised land.
